title: Abraham and Sarah Go to a New Land
bigQuestion: What does the Torah say Abraham and Sarah did when they left home, and how did they treat people?

story.title: Three Travelers in the Hot Sun
story.kicker: It is the hottest part of the day, and an old man runs to greet three strangers.
paragraphs: The sun is high. The sand is hot. An old man named Abraham sits at the door of his tent. He is resting in the shade. The Torah says he looks up. Three travelers are standing there.
Abraham does not wait. The Torah says he runs to them. He bows low. "Please stay," he says. "Rest under the tree. Let me bring water for your feet. Let me bring you bread."

Abraham hurries to the tent. "Sarah," he says, "quick, make bread!" Then he runs to the animals. He picks a calf for the meal. He brings milk and cheese too. He stands by the travelers while they eat.

The travelers have news. They say, "Next year, Sarah will have a son." Sarah is listening at the tent door. She laughs. She is very old. Can this be true? Jewish tradition tells this story every year.
story.think: Abraham ran to help strangers on a hot day. What do you do when a guest comes to your home?

lessons.title: Go to a New Land
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God told Abraham and Sarah to leave home and go to a new land, and they went.
reading: Abraham and Sarah lived in a place far away. Their first names were Abram and Sarai. The Torah says God spoke to Abram. God said, "Leave your land. Go to a land I will show you."
Abram did not know where he was going. He went anyway. Sarai went with him. So did his nephew Lot. They took their tents and their sheep. They walked a long way to a new *land*.
The new land was called Canaan. Jewish tradition says this is the land of Israel. Abraham and Sarah lived there in tents. They moved from place to place.

words.d: a place where people live; the Torah says Abraham went to a new land called Canaan

look.title: Go From Your Land
look.text: Now the LORD said unto Abram: 'Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father's house, unto the land that I will show thee.
look.prompt: "Get thee out" is an old way to say "go." What three things does the story say Abram had to leave?

check.q: What does the Torah say God told Abram to do?
choices: Leave his land and go to a new one
check.why: Genesis 12 says God told Abram to leave his land and go to a land God would show him.

check.q: Who went with Abram on the trip?
check.why: Sarai, his wife, and Lot, his nephew, went with him. Noah and Joseph are in other stories.

check.q: What was the new land called?
check.why: The land was called Canaan. Jewish tradition calls it the land of Israel.

lessons.title: A Promise of a Big Family
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says God promised Abraham and Sarah a very big family.
reading: Abraham and Sarah had no children. They were getting old. The Torah says God made them a *promise*. God said, "Your family will be big. It will be as many as the stars."
The story says God told Abram to look up at the night sky. Try to count the stars! You cannot. That is how big the family would be.
God gave them new names, the story says. Abram became Abraham. Sarai became Sarah. Jewish tradition says the new names were part of the promise.

words.d: something you say you will do, and then you do it
the man the Torah says left home for a new land; his first name was Abram

look.title: Count the Stars
look.text: Picture a dark night far from the city. There are no street lights. Look up. Stars fill the whole sky. Small ones, bright ones, more and more. The Torah says God told Abram his family would be as many as the stars.
look.prompt: Why do you think the story uses stars to talk about a big family?

check.q: What did God promise Abraham, in the story?
check.why: The Torah says God promised Abraham a family as many as the stars.

check.q: What was Sarah's name before it was Sarah?
check.why: Sarai became Sarah. Rebekah and Rachel are other women in the Torah.

check.q: What did the story tell Abram to look at?
check.why: Genesis 15 says God told Abram to look at the stars and try to count them.

lessons.title: Three Visitors
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Abraham ran to feed three strangers who came to his tent.
reading: One hot day, three travelers came by. Abraham did not know them. The Torah says he ran to meet them. He bowed. He asked them to rest and eat.
Abraham and Sarah made a big meal. Bread, milk, cheese and meat. Abraham did not sit down. He stood by his *guests* while they ate.
The guests had a message. Sarah would have a baby boy. Sarah laughed. She was very old. Jewish tradition says her laugh became the baby's name.

words.d: a person who comes to visit your home

look.title: He Ran to Meet Them
look.text: The Torah says Abraham looked up and saw three men standing near him. He ran from the door of his tent to meet them. He bowed down to the ground.
look.cite: Genesis (Bereshit) 18:2, retold from the Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Abraham ran. He did not walk. What does that tell you about how he felt about guests?

check.q: How many travelers came to Abraham's tent?
check.why: Genesis 18 says three men came. Abraham ran to meet them.

check.q: What did Abraham do when he saw the travelers?
check.why: The Torah says Abraham ran to meet them and asked them to stay and eat.

check.q: What news did the guests bring?
choices: Abraham would get a new tent
check.why: The guests said Sarah would have a baby boy. Sarah laughed.

lessons.title: Kindness to Strangers
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish tradition says Abraham's tent was open on all sides so every guest could come in.
reading: A *stranger* is a person you do not know. Abraham did not know the three men. He helped them anyway. Jewish tradition says this is a big lesson.
An old Jewish story says Abraham's tent was open on all four sides. A guest could walk in from any way. No one had to go around. The story is a *midrash*. A midrash is a story that adds to the Torah.
Jewish families still welcome guests. On Shabbat, many families invite people to eat. They call it welcoming guests. It is a way to be like Abraham and Sarah.

words.d: a person you do not know yet
a story Jewish teachers tell to add to a Torah story

look.title: A Tent With Four Doors
look.text: Picture a tent in the desert. Most tents have one door. This tent has a door on every side. Front, back, left and right. A traveler from any road can see a way in. Jewish tradition tells this story about Abraham's tent.
look.prompt: Why would a tent with four doors be good for guests? What is one way our classroom could be like that tent?

check.q: What is a stranger?
choices: A person you do not know
check.why: A stranger is someone you do not know yet. Abraham helped strangers.

check.q: What does the midrash say about Abraham's tent?
choices: It was open on all sides
check.why: The midrash says the tent was open on all sides so any guest could come in.

check.q: What do many Jewish families do on Shabbat to be like Abraham?
check.why: Welcoming guests to a meal is a way Jewish families follow Abraham and Sarah.

lessons.title: Isaac Is Born
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Sarah had a son named Isaac, and his name means "he laughs."
reading: The Torah says the promise came true. Sarah had a baby boy. They named him *Isaac*. In Hebrew, his name is Yitzchak. It means "he laughs."
Sarah said, "God has made laughter for me." Everyone who heard the news would laugh with her. Abraham and Sarah were very old. The story says Abraham was one hundred.
Jewish families read this story on Rosh Hashanah. That is the Jewish New Year. They hear how Isaac was born.

words.d: the son of Abraham and Sarah; his Hebrew name means "he laughs"

look.title: Big Numbers in the Story
rows: Travelers who came to the tent
Sarah's age when Isaac was born
Abraham's age when Isaac was born
look.cite: Genesis 17:17, 18:2 and 21:5, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? Why do you think Sarah laughed?

check.q: What does the name Isaac mean?
check.why: Isaac, or Yitzchak, means "he laughs." Sarah laughed when she heard the news.

check.q: Who were Isaac's mother and father?
check.why: Isaac was the son of Sarah and Abraham. Rachel and Jacob come later.

check.q: When do Jewish families read the story of Isaac's birth?
check.why: The story of Isaac's birth is read on Rosh Hashanah, the Jewish New Year.

lessons.title: Rebekah at the Well
lessons.mainIdea: The Torah says Rebekah gave water to a stranger and his camels, and she became Isaac's wife.
reading: Isaac grew up. Abraham sent a helper to find Isaac a wife. The helper took ten *camels*. He stopped at a well. A well is a deep hole with water in it.
A girl named Rebekah came to the well. The helper asked for a drink. Rebekah gave him water. Then she said, "I will get water for your camels too." Ten camels drink a lot!
The helper knew she was kind. Rebekah went with him. She married Isaac. Jewish tradition says Rebekah was kind like Abraham.

words.d: a big desert animal with a hump that can go a long time without water
a deep hole in the ground where people get water

look.title: Water for the Camels
look.text: Picture a well with a bucket on a rope. A tired man stands next to ten camels. A girl lowers the bucket. She pulls it up. She pours. Then she lowers it again. And again. The Torah says Rebekah did this until all the camels had drunk.
look.prompt: Rebekah did not have to water the camels. Why do you think she did it?

check.q: Where did the helper meet Rebekah?
check.why: Genesis 24 says the helper met Rebekah at a well.

check.q: What did Rebekah give the camels?
check.why: Rebekah drew water for the man and for all ten camels.

check.q: Who did Rebekah marry?
check.why: Rebekah became Isaac's wife. Abraham was his father and Lot was his cousin.

lessons.title: The First of the Family
lessons.mainIdea: Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first mother and father of the Jewish people.
reading: Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first of the family. In Hebrew, Abraham is called Avraham Avinu. That means "Abraham our father." Sarah is Sarah Imenu, "Sarah our mother."
Isaac and Rebekah come next. Then their children. Then their children's children. Jewish tradition says the whole Jewish people is one big *family*.
Jewish prayers name Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Many prayers name Sarah, Rebekah, Rachel and Leah too. The story of the family goes on.

words.d: people who belong together; Jewish tradition calls Abraham and Sarah the first of its family

look.title: The Family Grows
look.cite: Genesis 21 and 25, Jewish Publication Society translation, 1917
look.prompt: Isaac and Rebekah had two sons. Who do you think they were? The next chapter will tell you.

check.q: What does Avraham Avinu mean?
check.why: Avinu means "our father." Jewish tradition calls Abraham the father of the family.

check.q: Who does Jewish tradition call the first mother of the family?
check.why: Sarah is called Sarah Imenu, "Sarah our mother." Rebekah and Rachel came after her.

check.q: Which three men are named in many Jewish prayers?
check.why: Jewish prayers name Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, the fathers of the family.

review.q: What does the Torah say God told Abram and Sarai to do?
choices: Leave home and go to a new land
review.why: Genesis 12 says God told Abram to leave his land and go to a land God would show him.

review.q: The story says Abraham's family would be as many as what?
review.why: Genesis 15 says the family would be as many as the stars in the sky.

review.q: What did Abraham do when three strangers came?
choices: He ran to give them food
review.why: Genesis 18 says Abraham ran to meet them and gave them a big meal.

choices: A story that adds to a Torah story
review.why: A midrash is a story Jewish teachers tell to add to the Torah. One says Abraham's tent was open on all sides.

review.q: What does the name Isaac mean?
review.why: Isaac, or Yitzchak, means "he laughs." Sarah laughed when she heard she would have a son.

review.q: What kind thing did Rebekah do at the well?
choices: She gave water to a man and his camels
review.why: Genesis 24 says Rebekah gave water to the helper and to all his camels.
